item.title: VCF 9.1.2 is out
item.description: Broadcom shipped VCF 9.1.2 today. Most of it is about getting AI and Kubernetes platforms running faster, plus two features moving from tech preview to GA. Quickstarts. Some background: Supervisor is the Kubernetes control plane built into vSphere, and VKS (vSphere Kubernetes Service) uses it to…

item.title: New on vCloudOne: sizing calculators
item.description: I've added three sizing calculators to the site, one each for Amazon EVS, VMware Cloud on AWS and on-prem VCF. All three take the same input: RVTools exports, or workload totals typed in by hand. From there they work out how many hosts you need for CPU, memory and storage, add the management…

item.title: Amazon EVS, one year in
item.description: Amazon EVS went GA a little over a year ago. Here's what changed since, what I think matters most, and what to look at if you're planning a move.

item.title: SDDC 1.26v5 is the new default build
item.description: SDDC 1.26v5 is now the default build for new VMware Cloud on AWS SDDCs and upgrades. It's a security patch release with no new features. If you track SDDC versions for compliance, note it; otherwise it'll arrive with your normal upgrade schedule.

item.title: You can now raise the Elastic DRS storage warning
item.description: You can now raise the Elastic DRS storage warning on VMware Cloud on AWS from 65% up to 75%. What Elastic DRS does. Elastic DRS watches each cluster's CPU, memory and storage and adds or removes hosts based on policy. Storage is the one with a hard edge: vSAN needs free space for rebuilds and…

item.title: Amazon EVS gets r7i hosts, external principal storage and an Agent Skill
item.description: Amazon EVS now supports r7i.metal-24xl and r7i.metal-48xl hosts for VCF 9.x, external principal storage on Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, and an Agent Skill for AI assistants. r7i hosts. These are memory-optimized hosts on 4th Gen Intel Xeon (Sapphire Rapids): r7i.metal-24xl: 48 cores, 768 GiB…

item.title: vSphere Express, Live Recovery and DR built into VCF
item.description: Broadcom announced three changes to the VCF portfolio in early November. vSphere Express. A new entry edition built on vSphere 9, for customers with up to 128 cores across all their environments. It includes vMotion, High Availability (VMs restart on another host if one fails), the Distributed…

item.title: Amazon EVS adds Osaka, Taipei, Spain and Tel Aviv
item.description: Amazon EVS added four more Regions: Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Taipei), Europe (Spain) and Israel (Tel Aviv). Count December's seven and July's three, and that's fourteen new Regions in under a year. EVS environments live in a single Availability Zone, so resilience against a Regional…

item.title: VCF 9.1.1 lands the week of VMware Explore
item.description: VCF 9.1.1 shipped the same week as VMware Explore in Las Vegas. Most of what's new is aimed at private AI and platform teams. Multi-tenant model sharing. In VCF Private AI Services, one AI model deployment can now be shared by several tenants or business units. Each gets controlled access to the…

item.title: i7i.metal-48xl and the EVS Deployment Orchestrator
item.description: Two launches landed around Amazon EVS's first birthday: a bigger i7i host, and a tool that deploys a full VCF 9 environment from one CloudFormation stack. i7i.metal-48xl. It's double the 24xl: 96 physical cores on 5th Gen Intel Xeon, 1,536 GiB of memory, twelve 3.75 TB NVMe drives and 100 Gbps of…

item.title: Three good reads: NSX Federation, DR and memory tiering on EVS
item.description: In one week in August, AWS published three design posts for Amazon EVS. Together they cover the questions that come up once a migration is done. NSX Federation (Aug 18). Federation joins several NSX deployments under one Global Manager. You define segments, gateways and distributed firewall rules…

item.title: SDDC 1.26v4 is the new default build
item.description: SDDC 1.26v4 is now the default build for new VMware Cloud on AWS SDDCs and upgrades. It's a security patch release with no new features and nothing to configure. Existing SDDCs pick it up through the normal upgrade schedule.

item.title: Amazon EVS arrives in Seoul, Zurich and Stockholm
item.description: Amazon EVS is now in Asia Pacific (Seoul), Europe (Zurich) and Europe (Stockholm), with every existing feature, VCF 9.0 and 9.1 included. All three matter for data residency. Korea, Switzerland and Sweden each have customers, often in financial services and the public sector, whose data has to stay…

item.title: Amazon EVS now runs VCF 9.0 and 9.1
item.description: This is the big one for Amazon EVS this year. You can now run VCF 9.0 and 9.1 in every Region where EVS is available. What changed in the model. With VCF 5.2, EVS deployed the whole stack for you: hosts, networking, vCenter, NSX, vSAN and SDDC Manager. With VCF 9, the work is split. EVS provisions…

item.title: SDDC 1.26v3: fixes and Secure Boot certificate updates
item.description: SDDC 1.26v3 is a maintenance release for VMware Cloud on AWS, with quality and stability fixes. It's also the first release to deal with an expiring Microsoft Secure Boot certificate. Secure Boot checks that each piece of boot code is signed by a trusted key before it runs. Many of the keys VMs…

item.title: You can now take EVS VCF issues straight to Broadcom
item.description: Until now every Amazon EVS support case went through AWS, whatever the problem was. Now customers with an active VCF subscription can also open VCF software cases directly with Broadcom. How the two paths split: AWS Support still covers everything: EC2 hosts, VPC networking, the EVS service and…

item.title: Amazon EVS environments can now grow to 32 hosts
item.description: The host limit for an Amazon EVS environment went from 16 to 32. You get there by asking for a service quota increase, and it's available in every EVS Region. An EVS environment is one VCF instance: one management domain with vCenter, NSX, SDDC Manager and VCF Operations, and the hosts and clusters…

item.title: VCF 9.1 is here
item.description: Broadcom announced VCF 9.1 on May 5, the first feature release after 9.0. These are the parts I'd look at first. Memory tiering grows up. Memory tiering lets ESX use local NVMe as a second, slower tier of memory. A tiering engine watches which memory pages VMs actually use. Busy ("hot") pages stay…

item.title: Amazon EVS adds the i7i.metal-24xl
item.description: Amazon EVS now supports i7i.metal-24xl, a smaller host than the i4i.metal it launched with, on a newer CPU. How they compare: i4i.metal: 3rd Gen Intel Xeon (Ice Lake), 64 physical cores, 1,024 GiB of memory and eight 3.75 TB NVMe drives. i7i.metal-24xl: 5th Gen Xeon (Emerald Rapids), 48 physical…

item.title: Windows Server licenses on Amazon EVS
item.description: You can now license Windows Server through AWS for VMs running on Amazon EVS, and pay per vCPU-hour while each VM runs. Why it's needed. Running Windows Server on dedicated hosts in the cloud depends on license portability. Licenses with portability rights can be brought to EVS (BYOL), and AWS…

item.title: Usage Report APIs for VMware Cloud on AWS
item.description: VMware Cloud on AWS now has three usage report APIs, so you can pull consumption data into your own tools instead of waiting for the invoice. They all follow the same pattern, GET /activityanalytic/{org_id}/<type/{freq}/usage-report, return daily data, and accept up to 31 days per call: Host usage…

item.title: HCX 4.11.4 for VMware Cloud on AWS
item.description: HCX 4.11.4 is a maintenance release for VMware Cloud on AWS. Like 4.11.3, it ships without the WAN optimization appliance. WAN-OPT used to sit in an HCX service mesh and compress and dedupe migration traffic, which mattered on slow or expensive links. On a fast Direct Connect link it added little…

item.title: i7i.metal-24xl comes to VMware Cloud on AWS
item.description: With SDDC 1.26v2, VMware Cloud on AWS supports a new host type, i7i.metal-24xl, for new SDDCs and existing ones. What the host is. It runs on 5th Gen Intel Xeon (Emerald Rapids), with 48 physical cores and hyper-threading on by default, so vSphere sees 96 logical CPUs. It has 768 GiB of DDR5…

item.title: Amazon EVS deployment prerequisites guide
item.description: I wrote up everything Amazon EVS checks before it will deploy VCF 5.x, in the order you'll need it. EVS validates a lot before it builds anything: the account and support plan, IAM permissions, the VPC and its subnets, the service access subnet, Route 53 zones and records for every host and…

item.title: Multiple NSX Tier-0 gateways on Amazon EVS
item.description: Amazon EVS now supports more than one NSX Tier-0 gateway in an environment, each on its own NSX Edge cluster. Some background first. In NSX, VMs connect to overlay segments, and segments attach to Tier-1 gateways, which handle routing between those segments. The Tier-0 gateway sits above them and…

item.title: VCF 9.0.2 maintenance release
item.description: VCF 9.0.2 is mostly a fix release, but two changes in vCenter 9.0.2 remove common causes of trouble. Certificates renew themselves. vCenter and ESX use TLS certificates that the built-in VMware Certificate Authority (VMCA) issues. When they expire, things break: hosts disconnect, logins fail, and…

item.title: Pick your VCF and ESX versions on Amazon EVS
item.description: Amazon EVS now lets you pick a supported combination of VCF and ESX versions instead of always getting whatever EVS deploys by default. This launch also added VCF 5.2.2 for new environments. It works through three APIs. GetVersions lists the combinations EVS supports. CreateEnvironment takes the…

item.title: SDDC 1.26: vSAN ESA, bring your own key and VM hardware 21
item.description: SDDC 1.26 moves VMware Cloud on AWS to vSphere 8.0 Update 3. It's the biggest platform release VMC has had in a while, and it changes how you size storage. vSAN ESA. vSAN has two architectures. The Original Storage Architecture (OSA) splits each host's drives into a cache tier and a capacity tier…

item.title: Amazon EVS adds seven Regions
item.description: Amazon EVS is now in seven more Regions: US West (N. California), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Canada West (Calgary), Europe (Milan), Mexico (Central) and South America (São Paulo). A quick reminder of how EVS uses a Region. item.title: VMware Cloud on AWS: December 2025 roundup
item.description: Broadcom's December roundup for VMware Cloud on AWS had four changes worth knowing about. Two of them affect how you design and pay for an SDDC. Smaller stretched clusters.
